Here \(a=2x^{2}\), \(b=\frac{3}{2x}\), \(n=8\), so the general term is \(t_{r+1}={}^{8}C_{r}\left(2x^{2}\right)^{8-r}\left(\frac{3}{2x}\right)^{r}\).
For the \(3^{\text{rd}}\) term, \(r=2\).
\(t_{3}={}^{8}C_{2}\left(2x^{2}\right)^{6}\left(\frac{3}{2x}\right)^{2}=28\cdot 64x^{12}\cdot\frac{9}{4x^{2}}\)
\(=28\cdot 64\cdot\frac{9}{4}\cdot x^{10}\)
The \(3^{\text{rd}}\) term is \(4032x^{10}\).

The general term is \(t_{r+1}={}^{11}C_{r}\left(x^{2}\right)^{11-r}\left(-\frac{4}{x^{3}}\right)^{r}\).
For the \(5^{\text{th}}\) term, \(r=4\).
\(t_{5}={}^{11}C_{4}\left(x^{2}\right)^{7}\left(-\frac{4}{x^{3}}\right)^{4}=330\cdot x^{14}\cdot\frac{256}{x^{12}}\)
\(=330\cdot 256\cdot x^{2}\)
The \(5^{\text{th}}\) term is \(84480x^{2}\).

The general term is \(t_{r+1}={}^{9}C_{r}\left(\frac{4x}{5}\right)^{9-r}\left(-\frac{5}{2x}\right)^{r}\).
For the \(7^{\text{th}}\) term, \(r=6\), which is even, so the sign is positive.
\(t_{7}={}^{9}C_{6}\left(\frac{4x}{5}\right)^{3}\left(-\frac{5}{2x}\right)^{6}=84\cdot\frac{64x^{3}}{125}\cdot\frac{15625}{64x^{6}}\)
\(=84\cdot 125\cdot\frac{1}{x^{3}}\)
The \(7^{\text{th}}\) term is \(\frac{10500}{x^{3}}\).

The general term is \(t_{r+1}={}^{12}C_{r}\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^{12-r}\left(a^{2}\right)^{r}\).
For the \(9^{\text{th}}\) term, \(r=8\).
\(t_{9}={}^{12}C_{8}\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^{4}\left(a^{2}\right)^{8}=495\cdot\frac{1}{81}\cdot a^{16}\)
The \(9^{\text{th}}\) term is \(\frac{55a^{16}}{9}\).

The general term is \(t_{r+1}={}^{9}C_{r}\left(x^{2}\right)^{9-r}\left(\frac{3\sqrt{2}}{x}\right)^{r}={}^{9}C_{r}\left(3\sqrt{2}\right)^{r}x^{18-2r-r}\).
Collecting the power of \(x\), the general term carries \(x^{18-3r}\). For \(x^{3}\), set \(18-3r=3\), so \(r=5\).
Coefficient \(={}^{9}C_{5}\left(3\sqrt{2}\right)^{5}=126\cdot 3^{5}\cdot\left(\sqrt{2}\right)^{5}=126\cdot 243\cdot 4\sqrt{2}\)
The coefficient of \(x^{3}\) is \(122472\sqrt{2}\).

The general term is \(t_{r+1}={}^{8}C_{r}\left(2x^{5}\right)^{8-r}\left(-\frac{5}{x^{3}}\right)^{r}={}^{8}C_{r}\,2^{8-r}(-5)^{r}x^{40-5r-3r}\).
Collecting the power of \(x\), the general term carries \(x^{40-8r}\). For \(x^{8}\), set \(40-8r=8\), so \(r=4\).
Coefficient \(={}^{8}C_{4}\cdot 2^{4}\cdot(-5)^{4}=70\cdot 16\cdot 625\)
The coefficient of \(x^{8}\) is \(700000\).

The general term is \(t_{r+1}={}^{18}C_{r}\left(\frac{1}{x}\right)^{18-r}\left(x^{2}\right)^{r}={}^{18}C_{r}\,x^{-(18-r)+2r}\).
Collecting the power of \(x\), the general term carries \(x^{3r-18}\). For \(x^{9}\), set \(3r-18=9\), so \(r=9\).
Coefficient \(={}^{18}C_{9}\)
The coefficient of \(x^{9}\) is \(48620\).

The general term is \(t_{r+1}={}^{5}C_{r}\,x^{5-r}\left(-\frac{1}{2x}\right)^{r}={}^{5}C_{r}\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)^{r}x^{5-r-r}\).
Collecting the power of \(x\), the general term carries \(x^{5-2r}\). For \(x^{-3}\), set \(5-2r=-3\), so \(r=4\).
Coefficient \(={}^{5}C_{4}\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)^{4}=5\cdot\frac{1}{16}\)
The coefficient of \(x^{-3}\) is \(\frac{5}{16}\).

The general term is \(t_{r+1}={}^{15}C_{r}\left(x^{3}\right)^{15-r}\left(-\frac{1}{2x^{2}}\right)^{r}={}^{15}C_{r}\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)^{r}x^{45-3r-2r}\).
Collecting the power of \(x\), the general term carries \(x^{45-5r}\). For \(x^{-20}\), set \(45-5r=-20\), so \(r=13\).
Coefficient \(={}^{15}C_{13}\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)^{13}=105\cdot\left(-\frac{1}{8192}\right)\)
The coefficient of \(x^{-20}\) is \(-\frac{105}{8192}\).

The general term is \(t_{r+1}={}^{9}C_{r}\left(2x\right)^{9-r}\left(\frac{1}{3x^{2}}\right)^{r}={}^{9}C_{r}\,2^{9-r}\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^{r}x^{9-r-2r}\).
Collecting the power of \(x\), the general term carries \(x^{9-3r}\). For the term independent of \(x\), set \(9-3r=0\), so \(r=3\).
\(t_{4}={}^{9}C_{3}\cdot 2^{6}\cdot\frac{1}{27}=84\cdot\frac{64}{27}=\frac{5376}{27}\)
The constant term is \(\frac{1792}{9}\).

The general term is \(t_{r+1}={}^{15}C_{r}\,x^{15-r}\left(-\frac{2}{x^{2}}\right)^{r}={}^{15}C_{r}(-2)^{r}x^{15-r-2r}\).
Collecting the power of \(x\), the general term carries \(x^{15-3r}\). For the term independent of \(x\), set \(15-3r=0\), so \(r=5\).
\(t_{6}={}^{15}C_{5}(-2)^{5}=3003\cdot(-32)\)
The constant term is \(-96096\).

The general term is \(t_{r+1}={}^{10}C_{r}\left(\sqrt{x}\right)^{10-r}\left(-\frac{3}{x^{2}}\right)^{r}={}^{10}C_{r}(-3)^{r}x^{\frac{10-r}{2}-2r}\).
For the term independent of \(x\), set \(\frac{10-r}{2}-2r=0\), that is \(10-r-4r=0\), so \(r=2\).
\(t_{3}={}^{10}C_{2}(-3)^{2}=45\cdot 9\)
The constant term is \(405\).

[Textbook misprint in the stem, answer-affecting: the stem and the printed key contradict each other. As printed the expression is \(\left(x^2 - \dfrac{1}{x}\right)^8\), whose general term is \({}^{8}C_{r}\left(x^2\right)^{8-r}\left(-\dfrac{1}{x}\right)^{r}\), carrying \(x^{16-3r}\). Setting \(16 - 3r = 0\) gives \(r = \dfrac{16}{3}\), not an integer, so NO term is free of \(x\) — the exponents run \(16, 13, 10, 7, 4, 1, -2, -5, -8\). The key gives \(84\), which is exactly \({}^{9}C_{6}\), the constant term of the NINTH power. The printed index was checked at high zoom and our transcription is faithful: part (iv) prints a closed-loop \(8\) while part (v) directly below it prints an open-tailed \(9\) in the same crop, so the typesetting distinguishes the two digits. With index \(9\) the working is \(18 - 3r = 0\), \(r = 6\), \(t_{7} = {}^{9}C_{6} = 84\), which is the printed key.]

The general term is \(t_{r+1}={}^{8}C_{r}\left(x^{2}\right)^{8-r}\left(-\frac{1}{x}\right)^{r}={}^{8}C_{r}(-1)^{r}x^{16-2r-r}\).
Collecting the power of \(x\), the general term carries \(x^{16-3r}\). For a term independent of \(x\), set \(16-3r=0\), which gives \(r=\frac{16}{3}\).
But \(r\) must be an integer with \(0\le r\le 8\), and \(\frac{16}{3}\) is not an integer, so no value of \(r\) makes the power of \(x\) zero. Indeed the powers occurring are \(16,13,10,7,4,1,-2,-5,-8\), and \(0\) is not among them.
There is no constant term in this expansion.
_note: BOOK DEFECT (stem and key disagree). The printed key answers 84 for this part, but 84 is \({}^{9}C_{6}\), which is the constant term of \(\left(x^{2}-\frac{1}{x}\right)^{9}\), not of the printed 8th power. Our stem is FAITHFUL: the exponent was read at high zoom on out/binomial-theorem-11/p-11.png (printed p.80), where part (iv) prints a closed-loop 8 while part (v) directly below prints an open-tailed 9 in the same crop, so the two glyphs are distinguishable and (iv) is unambiguously 8. Verified by full sympy expansion: with index 8 the exponents are all congruent to 1 mod 3 and the constant term is 0; with index 9 the working is 18-3r=0, r=6, t7 = 9C6 = 84, exactly the printed key. So either the book's stem should read 9 or its key is stale. Answered as printed; the maintainer should adjudicate.

solution:
The general term is \(t_{r+1}={}^{9}C_{r}\left(2x^{2}\right)^{9-r}\left(-\frac{5}{x}\right)^{r}={}^{9}C_{r}\,2^{9-r}(-5)^{r}x^{18-2r-r}\).
Collecting the power of \(x\), the general term carries \(x^{18-3r}\). For the term independent of \(x\), set \(18-3r=0\), so \(r=6\).
\(t_{7}={}^{9}C_{6}\cdot 2^{3}\cdot(-5)^{6}=84\cdot 8\cdot 15625\)
The constant term is \(10500000\).

Here \(n=12\) is even, so the expansion has only ONE middle term, namely the \(\left(\frac{n}{2}+1\right)^{\text{th}}=7^{\text{th}}\) term, given by \(r=6\).
\(t_{7}={}^{12}C_{6}\left(\frac{x}{y}\right)^{6}\left(\frac{y}{x}\right)^{6}=924\cdot\frac{x^{6}}{y^{6}}\cdot\frac{y^{6}}{x^{6}}\)
The middle term is \(924\).

Here \(n=7\) is odd, so the expansion has TWO middle terms, namely the \(\left(\frac{n+1}{2}\right)^{\text{th}}=4^{\text{th}}\) and the \(\left(\frac{n+3}{2}\right)^{\text{th}}=5^{\text{th}}\) terms, given by \(r=3\) and \(r=4\).
\(t_{4}={}^{7}C_{3}\left(x^{2}\right)^{4}\left(\frac{1}{x}\right)^{3}=35\cdot\frac{x^{8}}{x^{3}}=35x^{5}\)
\(t_{5}={}^{7}C_{4}\left(x^{2}\right)^{3}\left(\frac{1}{x}\right)^{4}=35\cdot\frac{x^{6}}{x^{4}}=35x^{2}\)
The middle terms are \(35x^{5}\) and \(35x^{2}\).

Here \(n=8\) is even, so the expansion has only ONE middle term, namely the \(\left(\frac{n}{2}+1\right)^{\text{th}}=5^{\text{th}}\) term, given by \(r=4\).
\(t_{5}={}^{8}C_{4}\left(x^{2}\right)^{4}\left(-\frac{2}{x}\right)^{4}=70\cdot x^{8}\cdot\frac{16}{x^{4}}\)
The middle term is \(1120x^{4}\).

Here \(n=10\) is even, so the expansion has only ONE middle term, namely the \(\left(\frac{n}{2}+1\right)^{\text{th}}=6^{\text{th}}\) term, given by \(r=5\).
\(t_{6}={}^{10}C_{5}\left(\frac{x}{a}\right)^{5}\left(-\frac{a}{x}\right)^{5}=252\cdot(-1)\cdot\frac{x^{5}}{a^{5}}\cdot\frac{a^{5}}{x^{5}}\)
The middle term is \(-252\).

Here \(n=11\) is odd, so the expansion has TWO middle terms, namely the \(\left(\frac{n+1}{2}\right)^{\text{th}}=6^{\text{th}}\) and the \(\left(\frac{n+3}{2}\right)^{\text{th}}=7^{\text{th}}\) terms, given by \(r=5\) and \(r=6\).
\(t_{6}={}^{11}C_{5}\left(x^{4}\right)^{6}\left(-\frac{1}{x^{3}}\right)^{5}=462\cdot x^{24}\cdot\left(-\frac{1}{x^{15}}\right)=-462x^{9}\)
\(t_{7}={}^{11}C_{6}\left(x^{4}\right)^{5}\left(-\frac{1}{x^{3}}\right)^{6}=462\cdot x^{20}\cdot\frac{1}{x^{18}}=462x^{2}\)
The middle terms are \(-462x^{9}\) and \(462x^{2}\).

In \((k+x)^{8}\) the general term is \(t_{r+1}={}^{8}C_{r}\,k^{8-r}x^{r}\).
Taking \(r=5\), the coefficient of \(x^{5}\) is \({}^{8}C_{5}k^{3}=56k^{3}\); taking \(r=6\), the coefficient of \(x^{6}\) is \({}^{8}C_{6}k^{2}=28k^{2}\).
Given \(56k^{3}=10\left(28k^{2}\right)\), so \(56k^{3}=280k^{2}\), that is \(56k^{2}(k-5)=0\).
The root \(k=0\) is rejected, since it makes both coefficients \(0\).
\(k=5\)

In \((3x+1)^{9}\) the general term is \(t_{r+1}={}^{9}C_{r}\left(3x\right)^{r}(1)^{9-r}={}^{9}C_{r}\,3^{r}x^{r}\), so the coefficient of \(x^{r}\) is \({}^{9}C_{r}3^{r}\).
On multiplying by \((2-x)\), a term in \(x^{6}\) arises in two ways: \(2\) times the \(x^{6}\) term, and \(-x\) times the \(x^{5}\) term.
Coefficient of \(x^{6}=2\cdot{}^{9}C_{6}\cdot 3^{6}-{}^{9}C_{5}\cdot 3^{5}=2\cdot 84\cdot 729-126\cdot 243=122472-30618\)
The term containing \(x^{6}\) is \(91854x^{6}\).

The general term of \((1+2x)^{m}\) is \(t_{r+1}={}^{m}C_{r}\left(2x\right)^{r}={}^{m}C_{r}\,2^{r}x^{r}\), so the coefficient of \(x^{2}\) is \({}^{m}C_{2}\cdot 2^{2}\).
Given \({}^{m}C_{2}\cdot 4=112\), so \({}^{m}C_{2}=28\), that is \(\frac{m(m-1)}{2}=28\).
\(m^{2}-m-56=0\), so \((m-8)(m+7)=0\).
Since \(m\) is a positive integer, \(m=-7\) is rejected.
\(m=8\)
